name: @kitchensink/food-service-infra
//: ⛔ DELIBERATELY NOT AN npm WORKSPACE — absent from the root `workspaces` globs on purpose.
CDK is not part of the workspace installs. `aws-cdk-lib` is 149 MB and is a runtime dependency of no
service; while it was declared on the service it hoisted to the root tree, was pulled into
`turbo prune`, and shipped inside the service's container image.
This directory installs its own `node_modules`. Node resolves upward, so the CDK app finds aws-cdk-lib
here and still finds the `@kitchensink/*` workspace packages at the repo root.
⚠️ `@radicle-co/infra-shared` peers on aws-cdk-lib and owns no copy, so the constructs resolve THIS
directory's instance. Two instances is not a packaging nuisance: SecretValue tokens minted by one are
unresolvable by a stack from the other, and tsc rejects the assignment outright.
⚠️ CI pins the exact prerelease the run published (`cdk-checks`, `_ci.yml`), so a PR that changes a
shared construct is built and deployed against ITS OWN construct rather than the last published one.
⛔ `@kitchensink/messaging` is IMPORTED but deliberately NOT DECLARED. It is an unpublished workspace
package; declaring it here would make `npm install` in this directory resolve it from the registry
and 404. Node finds it by walking up to the repo root, where the workspace link lives. That is a
phantom dependency and it is the price of a CDK app sitting outside the workspace it belongs to —
recorded here rather than left for the next reader to discover through a failing install.

scripts.deploy: npm run bundle:lambda --prefix .. && cdk deploy --app 'npx tsx bin/app.ts'
scripts.synth: npm run bundle:lambda --prefix .. && cdk synth --app 'npx tsx bin/app.ts'
